Local well-posedness of the 1d compressible Navier–Stokes system with rough data

Ke Chen,   Ruilin Hu,   Quoc-Hung Nguyen ††thanks: E-mail address: kchen18@fudan.edu.cn, Fudan University, 220 Handan Road, Yangpu, Shanghai, 200433, China.††thanks: E-mail address: huruilin16@mails.ucas.ac.cn, Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, 100190, China.††thanks: E-mail address: qhnguyen@amss.ac.cn, Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, 100190, China.
Abstract

This paper presents a new approach to the local well-posedness of the 1d compressible Navier–Stokes systems with rough initial data. Our approach is based on establishing some smoothing and Lipschitz-type estimates for the 1d parabolic equation with piecewise continuous coefficients.

1 Introduction

In this paper, we study the compressible Navier–Stokes equations in Lagrangian coordinates, which can be written as (see [16])

{vt−ux=0,ut+px=(μ​uxv)x,(e+12​u2)t+(p​u)x=(κv​θx+μv​u​ux)x.\left\{\begin{aligned} &v_{t}-u_{x}=0,\\ &u_{t}+p_{x}=\left(\frac{\mu u_{x}}{v}\right)_{x},\\ &(e+\frac{1}{2}u^{2})_{t}+({p}u)_{x}=\left(\frac{\kappa}{v}\theta_{x}+\frac{\mu}{v}uu_{x}\right)_{x}.\end{aligned}\right. (1.1)

Here we denote vv the specific volume, uu the velocity, pp the pressure, ee the specific internal energy, θ\theta the absolute temperature. And μ,κ>0\mu,\kappa>0 are viscosity and heat conductivity coefficients. The above equations describe the conservation of mass, momentum and energy, respectively.

We will consider two systems. The first system is the so-called p−p-system (see [16]), which is a general model of isentropic gas dynamics(when p⁡(v)=A​v−γp(v)=Av^{-\gamma}). In the isentropic case, the temperature is held constant hence energy must be added to the system, whence the conservation of energy is absent. The p−p-system can be written as

{vt−ux=0,ut+(p⁡(v))x=(μ​uxv)x.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{aligned} &v_{t}-u_{x}=0,\\ &u_{t}+(p(v))_{x}=(\frac{\mu u_{x}}{v})_{x}.\end{aligned}\right. (1.2)

In this paper we consider a more general system which only requires p∈W2,∞p\in W^{2,\infty}.

Another system studied in this paper is (1.1) for the polytropic ideal gas which has the constitutive relations

p⁡(v,θ)=K​θv,e=𝐜​θ,p(v,\theta)=\frac{K\theta}{v},\ \ \ e=\mathbf{c}\theta,

where KK and heat capacity 𝐜\mathbf{c} are both positive constants. The system can be written as

{vt−ux=0,ut+(p⁡(v,θ))x=(μ​uxv)x,θt+p⁡(v,θ)𝐜​ux−μ𝐜​v​(ux)2=(κ𝐜​v​θx)x.\left\{\begin{aligned} &v_{t}-u_{x}=0,\\ &u_{t}+(p(v,\theta))_{x}=\left(\frac{\mu u_{x}}{v}\right)_{x},\\ &\theta_{t}+\frac{p(v,\theta)}{\mathbf{c}}u_{x}-\frac{\mu}{\mathbf{c}v}(u_{x})^{2}=\left(\frac{\kappa}{\mathbf{c}v}\theta_{x}\right)_{x}.\end{aligned}\right. (1.3)

Let us give a review of classical results. The study about compressible Navier-Stokes equations in gas dynamics started with Nash in [15], where he considered general elliptic and parabolic equations. Then Itaya [5, 6] solved the compressible Navier-Stokes equations for initial data in Hölder space. Kazhikhov [9] established a priori estimates and proved the existence of weak and classical solutions. For the equation of 3-d ideal gas, Nishida and Matsumura in [12] applied the energy method to give the existence of a global solution with data in Hölder space. The result of large-time behavior of global solution was provided by Kawashima [8]. Using the energy method, Hoff [4] proved the existence of a global solution for discontinuous data. The results in the book of Lions [10] and the book of Feireisl [2] are applicable to a larger space of initial data.

Recently, Liu and Yu [11] studied the system (1.2) with B​V∩L1BV\cap L^{1} data, under the assumption p′​(v)<0p^{\prime}(v)<0. Based on exact analysis of the associated linear equations and their Green’s functions, they initiated a new method, which converts the differential equations into integral equations, and proved that for initial data v0,u0v_{0},u_{0} satisfying

‖v0−1‖L1,‖v0‖B​V,‖u0‖L1,‖u0‖B​V<δ≪1,\displaystyle\|v_{0}-1\|_{L^{1}},\|v_{0}\|_{BV},\|u_{0}\|_{L^{1}},\|u_{0}\|_{BV}<\delta\ll 1,

there exist t♯>0t_{\sharp}>0 and C♯>0C_{\sharp}>0 such that the system (1.2) admits a unique weak solution (v,u)(v,u) for t∈(0,t♯)t\in(0,t_{\sharp}), and

‖v⁡(t,⋅)−1‖L1+‖v⁡(t,⋅)‖B​V+‖t​ux​(t,⋅)‖L∞≤2​C♯​δ,∀t∈(0,t♯).\displaystyle\|v(t,\cdot)-1\|_{L^{1}}+\|v(t,\cdot)\|_{BV}+\|\sqrt{t}u_{x}(t,\cdot)\|_{L^{\infty}}\leq 2C_{\sharp}\delta,\ \ \ \forall t\in(0,t_{\sharp}).

Moreover, they also established global result for polytropic gases p⁡(v)=A​v−γp(v)=Av^{-\gamma} with 1≤γ<e1\leq\gamma<e. Their result was extended to the full compressible Navier–Stokes system (1.3) by Wang, Yu, and Zhang [18].

In this paper, we are interested in the local well-posedness of (1.2) and (1.3) with rough data, which allows v0v_{0} to have a finite jump. The idea to study the elliptic problem with jump coefficients comes from [13, 14]. More precisely, without loss of generality, let x=0x=0 be the jump point. Suppose there exists ε>0\varepsilon>0 such that

|v0​(x)−v0​(y)|≤δ,if​|x−y|≤ε​and​x​y>0,\displaystyle|v_{0}(x)-v_{0}(y)|\leq\delta,\ \ \ \text{if}\ |x-y|\leq\varepsilon\ \text{and}\ xy>0, (1.4)

for some δ>0\delta>0 that will be fixed later.

Throughout the paper, we fix two constants 0<α<γ≪10<\alpha<\gamma\ll 1. Define the norms

‖f‖XTσ,p​(E)=sup0<s<Tsσ​‖f⁡(s)‖Lp​(E)+sup0<s<t<Tsσ+α​‖f⁡(t)−f⁡(s)‖Lp​(E)(t−s)α,\displaystyle\|f\|_{X_{T}^{\sigma,p}(E)}=\sup_{0<s<T}s^{\sigma}\|f(s)\|_{L^{p}(E)}+\sup_{0<s<t<T}s^{\sigma+\alpha}\frac{\|f(t)-f(s)\|_{L^{p}(E)}}{(t-s)^{\alpha}},
‖f‖YT​(E)=sup0<s<T‖f⁡(s)‖L∞​(E)+sup0<s<t<Tsα​‖f⁡(t)−f⁡(s)‖L∞​(E)(t−s)α,\displaystyle\|f\|_{Y_{T}(E)}=\sup_{0<s<T}\|f(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(E)}+\sup_{0<s<t<T}s^{\alpha}\frac{\|f(t)-f(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(E)}}{(t-s)^{\alpha}},
‖f‖LTp​(E)=‖f‖LTp​(E)=(∫0T∫E|f⁡(t,x)|p​𝑑x​𝑑t)1p,for any measurable set​E⊆ℝ,\displaystyle\|f\|_{L^{p}_{T}(E)}=\|f\|_{L^{p}_{T}(E)}=\left(\int_{0}^{T}\int_{E}|f(t,x)|^{p}dxdt\right)^{\frac{1}{p}},\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \text{for any measurable set}\ E\subseteq\mathbb{R},

and we omit the domain if E=ℝE=\mathbb{R}. We write several norms together to denote the sum of them. Moreover, we denote A≲BA\lesssim B if there exists a universal constant CC such that A≤C​BA\leq CB. We will solve the system (1.2) and (1.3) by the fixed point theorem in the Banach space equipped with the norms above. We note that the norms ∥⋅∥XTσ,p\|\cdot\|_{X_{T}^{\sigma,p}} and ∥⋅∥YT\|\cdot\|_{Y_{T}} contain Hölder derivatives in time.

For the system (1.2), we impose the following conditions for initial data

v0∈L∞,infxv0≥λ0>0,u0=∂xu¯0​with⁡u¯0∈C˙2​γ.\displaystyle v_{0}\in L^{\infty},\ \inf_{x}v_{0}\geq\lambda_{0}>0,\ u_{0}=\partial_{x}\bar{u}_{0}\ \operatorname{with}\ \bar{u}_{0}\in\dot{C}^{2\gamma}. (1.5)

Simplified versions of our main results are stated in the following theorems.

Theorem 1.1

Assume p∈W2,∞​(ℝ)p\in W^{2,\infty}(\mathbb{R}). There exists δ0>0\delta_{0}>0 such that if initial data (v0,u0)(v_{0},u_{0}) satisfies the conditions (1.4) and (1.5) with δ=δ0\delta=\delta_{0}, then the system (1.2) admits a unique local solution (v,u)(v,u) in [0,T][0,T] satisfying

inft∈[0,T]infxv⁡(t,x)≥λ02,‖v‖YT≤2​‖v0‖L∞,‖∂xu‖XT1−γ,∞≤M,\displaystyle\inf_{t\in[0,T]}\inf_{x}v(t,x)\geq\frac{\lambda_{0}}{2},\ \ \ \|v\|_{Y_{T}}\leq 2\|v_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}},\ \ \ \ \|\partial_{x}u\|_{X_{T}^{1-\gamma,\infty}}\leq M,

for some T,M>0T,M>0.

For the full N–S system (1.3), we use LpL^{p} setting, and set the following norm and corresponding Banach space

‖(w,ϑ)‖ZT:=\displaystyle\|(w,\vartheta)\|_{Z_{T}}:= ∑⋆∈{LT2,XT12,2,XT34,∞}‖∂xw‖⋆+∑⋆∈{LT2,XT12,2}‖ϑ‖⋆+∑⋆∈{LT65,XT56,65}‖∂xϑ‖⋆.\displaystyle\sum_{\star\in\{L^{2}_{T},X_{T}^{\frac{1}{2},2},X_{T}^{\frac{3}{4},\infty}\}}\|\partial_{x}w\|_{\star}+\sum_{\star\in\{L^{2}_{T},X_{T}^{\frac{1}{2},2}\}}\|\vartheta\|_{\star}+\sum_{\star\in\{L^{\frac{6}{5}}_{T},X_{T}^{\frac{5}{6},\frac{6}{5}}\}}\|\partial_{x}\vartheta\|_{\star}.

The above norms have the same scaling in the parabolic setting. The norms ‖∂xw‖LT2\|\partial_{x}w\|_{L^{2}_{T}}, ‖ϑ‖LT2\|\vartheta\|_{L^{2}_{T}} and ‖∂xϑ‖LT65\|\partial_{x}\vartheta\|_{L^{\frac{6}{5}}_{T}} are imposed in view of the parabolic structure of the equation of (u,θ)(u,\theta). Other norms ‖∂xw‖XT12,2,‖∂xw‖XT34,∞,‖ϑ‖XT12,2,‖∂xϑ‖XT56,65\|\partial_{x}w\|_{X_{T}^{\frac{1}{2},2}},\|\partial_{x}w\|_{X_{T}^{\frac{3}{4},\infty}},\|\vartheta\|_{X_{T}^{\frac{1}{2},2}},\|\partial_{x}\vartheta\|_{X_{T}^{\frac{5}{6},\frac{6}{5}}} are necessary to obtain local estimates of vv.

We assume the initial data satisfies that

infxv0​(x)≥λ0>0,‖v0‖L∞<∞,‖u0‖L2<∞,‖θ0‖W˙−23,65<∞.\displaystyle\inf_{x}v_{0}(x)\geq\lambda_{0}>0,\ \ \ \|v_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}}<\infty,\ \ \|u_{0}\|_{L^{2}}<\infty,\ \ \|\theta_{0}\|_{\dot{W}^{-\frac{2}{3},\frac{6}{5}}}<\infty. (1.6)

The following result is the local well-posedness of system (1.3).

Theorem 1.2

There exists δ0>0\delta_{0}>0 such that if initial data (v0,u0,θ0)(v_{0},u_{0},\theta_{0}) satisfies (1.4) and (1.6) with δ=δ0\delta=\delta_{0}, then the system (1.3) has a unique local solution (v,u)(v,u) in [0,T][0,T] satisfying

inft∈[0,T]infxv⁡(t,x)≥λ02,‖v‖YT≤2​‖v0‖L∞,‖(u,θ)‖ZT≤B.\displaystyle\inf_{t\in[0,T]}\inf_{x}v(t,x)\geq\frac{\lambda_{0}}{2},\ \ \ \|v\|_{Y_{T}}\leq 2\|v_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}},\ \ \ \ \|(u,\theta)\|_{Z_{T}}\leq B.

for some T,B>0T,B>0.

Note that we do not need u0,θ0u_{0},\theta_{0} decay at infinity. Hence the condition (1.6) can be relaxed to local LpL^{p} norms(see Theorem 5.2):

infxv0​(x)≥λ0>0,‖v0‖L∞<∞,supz∈ℝ‖u0​χz‖L2<∞,supz∈ℝ‖θ0​χz‖W˙−23,65<∞.\displaystyle\inf_{x}v_{0}(x)\geq\lambda_{0}>0,\ \ \ \|v_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}}<\infty,\ \ \sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}}\|u_{0}\chi_{z}\|_{L^{2}}<\infty,\ \ \sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}}\|\theta_{0}\chi_{z}\|_{\dot{W}^{-\frac{2}{3},\frac{6}{5}}}<\infty. (1.7)

Here χz\chi_{z} is a smooth cutoff function satisfying 𝟏[z−1,z+1]≤χz≤𝟏[z−2,z+2]\mathbf{1}_{[z-1,z+1]}\leq\chi_{z}\leq\mathbf{1}_{[z-2,z+2]}, where 𝟏\mathbf{1} is the indicator function.

Our method is based on analysis of heat equation with jump coefficient ϕ⁡(x)\phi(x) satisfying (3.2),

∂tf⁡(t,x)−∂x(ϕ⁡(x)​∂xf⁡(t,x))=∂xF⁡(t,x)+R⁡(t,x),\displaystyle\partial_{t}f(t,x)-\partial_{x}(\phi(x)\partial_{x}f(t,x))=\partial_{x}F(t,x)+R(t,x),
f⁡(0,x)=f0​(x).\displaystyle f(0,x)=f_{0}(x).

We convert the differential equations into integral equations and give two different formulas of solution. One formula (3.9) is suitable for estimates near jump points, and another one (3.37) behaves well for estimates far from jump points. Our main results rely on Lemma 3.1.

We make some remarks about the choice of initial data. For the isentropic system (1.2), we requires u0∈B˙∞,∞−1+2​γu_{0}\in\dot{B}^{-1+2\gamma}_{\infty,\infty}. Generally in Schauder theory of parabolic/elliptic equations, to control the Lipschitz norm of solution, it requires the coefficient to be at least Dini (see [7]). Due to the roughness of coefficient, the space B˙∞,∞−1+2​γ\dot{B}^{-1+2\gamma}_{\infty,\infty} is optimal in the sense that we can take γ>0\gamma>0 arbitrarily close to 0. For the full N–S system (1.2), we require u0∈L2u_{0}\in L^{2} and θ0∈W˙−23,65\theta_{0}\in\dot{W}^{-\frac{2}{3},\frac{6}{5}}. Taking a glance at the equation of θ\theta, we need (ux)2,θ​ux∈LT1(u_{x})^{2},\theta u_{x}\in L^{1}_{T} to make θ\theta well-defined. By classical theory of heat equation, ux∈LT2u_{x}\in L^{2}_{T} requires u0∈L2u_{0}\in L^{2}, and θ∈LT2\theta\in L^{2}_{T} requires θ0∈H˙−1\theta_{0}\in\dot{H}^{-1}. Taking force terms into consideration, we finally choose θ0∈W˙−23,65⊂H˙−1\theta_{0}\in\dot{W}^{-\frac{2}{3},\frac{6}{5}}\subset\dot{H}^{-1}.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. We introduce some primary properties for heat equations and heat kernel in Section 2. We establish the main lemma 3.1 in Section 3. In Section 4 we apply Lemma 3.1 to obtain local well-posedness for system (1.2) and prove Theorem 1.1. Section 5 is devoted to prove local wellposedness for system (1.3) and prove Theorem 1.2.

2 Preliminaries

We introduce the following estimates for the standard heat kernel 𝐊⁡(t,x)=(4​π​t)−12​e−x24​t\mathbf{K}(t,x)=(4\pi t)^{-\frac{1}{2}}e^{-\frac{x^{2}}{4t}} in ℝ\mathbb{R} which satisfies

∂t𝐊⁡(t,x)−∂x​x𝐊⁡(t,x)=0,\displaystyle\partial_{t}\mathbf{K}(t,x)-\partial_{xx}\mathbf{K}(t,x)=0,
limt→0+𝐊⁡(t,x)=𝐃𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐜⁡(x).\displaystyle\lim_{t\to 0^{+}}\mathbf{K}(t,x)=\mathbf{Dirac}(x).

The following estimates for heat kernel will be used frequently in our proof.

Lemma 2.1

There holds

|∂tj∂xm𝐊⁡(t,x)|≲1(t12+|x|)1+2​j+m,\displaystyle|\partial_{t}^{j}\partial_{x}^{m}\mathbf{K}(t,x)|\lesssim\frac{1}{(t^{\frac{1}{2}}+|x|)^{1+2j+m}},
(∫0∞|∂xm𝐊⁡(t,x)|p​𝑑t)1p≲|x|2p−1−m,(∫ℝ|∂xm𝐊⁡(t,x)|p​𝑑x)1p≲t12​(1p−1−m),\displaystyle\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}|\partial_{x}^{m}\mathbf{K}(t,x)|^{p}dt\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}\lesssim|x|^{\frac{2}{p}-1-m},\ \ \ \ \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\partial_{x}^{m}\mathbf{K}(t,x)|^{p}dx\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}\lesssim t^{\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{p}-1-m)},
(∫ℝ|∂tj∂xm𝐊⁡(t,x)|p​|x|σ​p​𝑑x)1p≲1tj+12​(m−1p+1−σ),\displaystyle\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\partial_{t}^{j}\partial_{x}^{m}\mathbf{K}(t,x)|^{p}|x|^{\sigma p}dx\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}\lesssim\frac{1}{t^{j+{\frac{1}{2}(m-\frac{1}{p}+1-\sigma)}}},
(∫ℝ|∂tj∂xm𝐊⁡(t+a,x)−∂tj∂xm𝐊⁡(t,x)|p​|x|σ​p​𝑑x)1p≲1tj+12​(m−1p+1−σ)​min​{1,at},\displaystyle\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\partial_{t}^{j}\partial_{x}^{m}\mathbf{K}(t+a,x)-\partial_{t}^{j}\partial_{x}^{m}\mathbf{K}(t,x)|^{p}|x|^{\sigma p}dx\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}\lesssim\frac{1}{t^{j+{\frac{1}{2}(m-\frac{1}{p}+1-\sigma)}}}\min\{1,\frac{a}{t}\},

for any m,j=0,1,2m,j=0,1,2, any σ,a,t≥0\sigma,a,t\geq 0 and p∈[1,+∞]p\in[1,+\infty].

It is easy to check the above estimates by the definition of heat kernel and the fact that bme−b≲m1b^{m}e^{-b}\lesssim_{m}1, ∀b>0,m∈ℕ+\forall b>0,m\in\mathbb{N}^{+}. We omit details here.

Lemma 2.2

Let h∈W˙σ,p​(ℝ)h\in\dot{W}^{\sigma,p}(\mathbb{R}) for some σ∈(0,1),p∈[1,∞)\sigma\in(0,1),p\in[1,\infty). Define 𝐡⁡(x)=h⁡(x)​𝟏x≥0+h⁡(−x)​𝟏x<0\mathbf{h}(x)=h(x)\mathbf{1}_{x\geq 0}+h(-x)\mathbf{1}_{x<0} and 𝐡¯​(x)=(h⁡(x)−h⁡(−x))​𝟏x≤0\bar{\mathbf{h}}(x)=(h(x)-h(-x))\mathbf{1}_{x\leq 0}. Then we have

∫ℝ∫0∞|𝐡⁡(x)−𝐡⁡(x−z)|p​d​x​d​z|z|1+σ​p+∫ℝ∫0∞|𝐡¯​(x)−𝐡¯​(x−z)|p​d​x​d​z|z|1+σ​p≲‖h‖W˙σ,pp.\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{0}^{\infty}|\mathbf{h}(x)-\mathbf{h}(x-z)|^{p}\frac{dxdz}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}}+\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{0}^{\infty}|\bar{\mathbf{h}}(x)-\bar{\mathbf{h}}(x-z)|^{p}\frac{dxdz}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}}\lesssim\|h\|_{\dot{W}^{\sigma,p}}^{p}.

Proof. By definition, one can check that

|𝐡⁡(x)−𝐡⁡(x−z)|p|z|1+σ​p\displaystyle\frac{|\mathbf{h}(x)-\mathbf{h}(x-z)|^{p}}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}} =𝟏x≥z​|h⁡(x)−h⁡(x−z)|p|z|1+σ​p+𝟏x<z​|h⁡(x)−h⁡(z−x)|p|z|1+σ​p\displaystyle=\mathbf{1}_{x\geq z}\frac{|{h}(x)-{h}(x-z)|^{p}}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}}+\mathbf{1}_{x<z}\frac{|{h}(x)-{h}(z-x)|^{p}}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}}
≤|h⁡(x)−h⁡(x−z)|p|z|1+σ​p+|h⁡(x)−h⁡(z−x)|p|2​x−z|1+σ​p,\displaystyle\leq\frac{|{h}(x)-{h}(x-z)|^{p}}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}}+\frac{|{h}(x)-{h}(z-x)|^{p}}{|2x-z|^{1+\sigma p}},
|𝐡¯​(x)−𝐡¯​(x−z)|p|z|1+σ​p\displaystyle\frac{|\bar{\mathbf{h}}(x)-\bar{\mathbf{h}}(x-z)|^{p}}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}} =𝟏x<z​|h⁡(x−z)−h⁡(z−x)|p|z|1+σ​p\displaystyle=\mathbf{1}_{x<z}\frac{|{h}(x-z)-{h}(z-x)|^{p}}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}}
≤|h⁡(x)−h⁡(x−z)|p|z|1+σ​p+|h⁡(x)−h⁡(z−x)|p|2​x−z|1+σ​p.\displaystyle\leq\frac{|{h}(x)-{h}(x-z)|^{p}}{|z|^{1+\sigma p}}+\frac{|{h}(x)-{h}(z-x)|^{p}}{|2x-z|^{1+\sigma p}}.

The result is standard in view of the fact that

‖h‖W˙σ,pp=∬ℝ2|h⁡(x)−h⁡(y)|p|x−y|1+σ​p​𝑑x​𝑑y.\|h\|_{\dot{W}^{\sigma,p}}^{p}=\iint_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}\frac{|h(x)-h(y)|^{p}}{|x-y|^{1+\sigma p}}dxdy.

This completes the proof.  

We introduce the following Schauder type lemma, the idea can be found in [1].

Lemma 2.3

Let 𝐊\mathbf{K} be the heat kernel, and let

g⁡(t,x)=∫0t∫ℝ∂t𝐊⁡(t−τ,x−y)​f​(τ,y)​𝑑y​𝑑τ.\displaystyle g(t,x)=\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\partial_{t}\mathbf{K}(t-\tau,x-y)f(\tau,y)dyd\tau.

Then we have

‖g‖XTσ,p≲‖f‖XTσ,p,∀T>0,σ∈(0,1−α),p∈[1,∞].\displaystyle\|g\|_{X_{T}^{\sigma,p}}\lesssim\|f\|_{X_{T}^{\sigma,p}},\ \ \ \forall T>0,\ \sigma\in(0,1-\alpha),\ p\in[1,\infty]. (2.1)

Proof. One has

g⁡(t,x)\displaystyle g(t,x) =∫0t∫ℝ∂t𝐊⁡(t−τ,x−y)​(f⁡(τ,y)−f⁡(t,y))​𝑑y​𝑑τ+∫0t∫ℝ∂t𝐊⁡(t−τ,x−y)​f​(t,y)​𝑑y​𝑑τ\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\partial_{t}\mathbf{K}(t-\tau,x-y)(f(\tau,y)-f(t,y))dyd\tau+\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\partial_{t}\mathbf{K}(t-\tau,x-y)f(t,y)dyd\tau
:=g1​(t,x)+g2​(t,x).\displaystyle:=g_{1}(t,x)+g_{2}(t,x).

By Lemma 2.1 we get

‖g1​(t)‖Lp≲∫0t‖∂t𝐊⁡(t−τ)‖L1​‖f⁡(τ)−f⁡(t)‖Lp​𝑑τ≲∫0t(t−τ)α−1​τ−σ−α​𝑑τ​‖f‖XTσ,p≲t−σ​‖f‖XTσ,p.\displaystyle\|g_{1}(t)\|_{L^{p}}\lesssim\int_{0}^{t}\|\partial_{t}\mathbf{K}(t-\tau)\|_{L^{1}}\|f(\tau)-f(t)\|_{L^{p}}d\tau\lesssim\int_{0}^{t}(t-\tau)^{\alpha-1}\tau^{-\sigma-\alpha}d\tau\|f\|_{X_{T}^{\sigma,p}}\lesssim t^{-\sigma}\|f\|_{X_{T}^{\sigma,p}}.

Moreover, observe that ∫0t∂t𝐊⁡(t−τ,x−y)​𝑑τ=K⁡(t,x−y)−𝐃𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐜⁡(x−y)\int_{0}^{t}\partial_{t}\mathbf{K}(t-\tau,x-y)d\tau=K(t,x-y)-\mathbf{Dirac}(x-y), hence

g2​(t,x)=∫ℝ𝐊⁡(t,x−y)​f​(t,y)​𝑑y−f⁡(t,x).g_{2}(t,x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbf{K}(t,x-y)f(t,y)dy-f(t,x).

Then

We consider the system (1.2) and the system (1.3) with jump initial data v0v_{0}. Observe that the equation for vv is hyperbolic, v⁡(t)v(t) will have jump at some points for any t>0t>0. To deal with uu in (1.2) and (u,θ)(u,\theta) in (1.3), we need to consider the following parabolic equation with jump coefficient.

∂tf⁡(t,x)−∂x(ϕ⁡(x)​∂xf⁡(t,x))=∂xF⁡(t,x)+R⁡(t,x),\displaystyle\partial_{t}f(t,x)-\partial_{x}(\phi(x)\partial_{x}f(t,x))=\partial_{x}F(t,x)+R(t,x), (3.1)
f⁡(0,x)=f0​(x).\displaystyle f(0,x)=f_{0}(x).

The following is the Hardy’s inequality.

Lemma 3.4

For any non-negative measurable function h:ℝ→ℝ+h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{+}, there holds for any p∈(1,∞)p\in(1,\infty),

∫0∞(∫0∞h⁡(x)​d​xx+y)p​𝑑y≲∫0∞h​(x)p​𝑑x.\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}h(x)\frac{dx}{x+y}\right)^{p}dy\lesssim\int_{0}^{\infty}h(x)^{p}dx.

Proof. By Hardy’s inequality [3],

∫0∞(∫0∞h⁡(x)​d​xx+y)p​𝑑y≤\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}h(x)\frac{dx}{x+y}\right)^{p}dy\leq ∫0∞(∫0yh⁡(x)​𝑑x)p​d​yyp+∫0∞(∫y∞h⁡(x)​d​xx)p​𝑑y\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\int_{0}^{y}h(x){dx}\right)^{p}\frac{dy}{y^{p}}+\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\int_{y}^{\infty}h(x)\frac{dx}{x}\right)^{p}{dy}
≤\displaystyle\leq (pp(p−1)p+pp)​∫0∞h​(x)p​𝑑x.\displaystyle\left(\frac{p^{p}}{(p-1)^{p}}+p^{p}\right)\int_{0}^{\infty}h(x)^{p}dx.

This completes the proof.

‖∫0∞‖f⁡(y)‖Lt,Tq​d​y|x+y|1r‖Lxp​(ℝ+)≲‖f‖LTq​‖|x|−1r‖Lwr≲‖f‖LTq.\displaystyle\left\|\int_{0}^{\infty}\|f(y)\|_{L^{q}_{t,T}}\frac{dy}{|x+y|^{\frac{1}{r}}}\right\|_{L^{p}_{x}(\mathbb{R}^{+})}\lesssim\|f\|_{L^{q}_{T}}\||x|^{-\frac{1}{r}}\|_{L^{r}_{w}}\lesssim\|f\|_{L^{q}_{T}}.

and
